title: A ring map is flat if and only if it is ind-flat
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings in one universe and let $f:A\to B$ be a ring map. Then $f$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] if and only if it is a filtered colimit of flat ring maps out of $A$, with the colimit formed in the category of $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: RingHom.Flat.iff_ind_flat and CommRingCat.ind_flat_eq_flat; the module-colimit flatness argument is Stacks Tag 05UT, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05UT

proof.text: For the forward implication take the one-object diagram consisting of f. For the reverse implication forget the filtered algebra colimit to modules: the forgetful functors preserve filtered colimits [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Every stage is a flat A-module, so [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules] makes the underlying A-module of B flat. This is exactly flatness of f. The existing source proof implements this through ObjectProperty.ind_inverseImage_le and ModuleCat.ind_flat.
